articles.title: Personal data (definition)
articles.summary: Information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person, directly or through identifiers such as a name, identification number, location data or online identifier.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Pseudonymisation
articles.summary: Processing so that data cannot be attributed to a person without additional information kept separately; pseudonymised data remain personal data.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Genetic data
articles.summary: Personal data on the inherited or acquired genetic characteristics of a person that give unique information on their physiology or health.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Biometric data
articles.summary: Personal data from technical processing of physical, physiological or behavioural characteristics that allow or confirm unique identification, such as facial images.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Data concerning health
articles.summary: Personal data on a person's physical or mental health, including health care services, that reveal information about their health status.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Purpose limitation
articles.summary: Data are collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes and not further processed in a way that is incompatible with them.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-5-gdpr/ on 2026-10-14; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Data minimisation
articles.summary: Data must be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for the purposes of the processing.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-5-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Storage limitation
articles.summary: Data are kept in a form that identifies people for no longer than is necessary for the purposes.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-5-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Integrity and confidentiality
articles.summary: Data are processed with appropriate security, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing and against accidental loss, destruction or damage.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-5-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Accountability
articles.summary: The controller is responsible for, and must be able to demonstrate, compliance with the principles of the first paragraph.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-5-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Lawfulness of processing
articles.summary: Processing is lawful only with a legal basis: consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task or legitimate interests.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-6-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Child's consent for information society services
articles.summary: Applies to consent-based information society services offered directly to a child; the consent age is 16 and member states may lower it to no less than 13.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-8-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Special categories of data
articles.summary: Prohibits processing data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political, religious or philosophical beliefs, union membership, genetic or biometric data (for identification), health or sex life.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-9-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Exceptions for special categories
articles.summary: Lists the conditions that lift the prohibition, such as explicit consent, employment law, vital interests, health care or public health, and research.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-9-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Criminal convictions and offences
articles.summary: Processing data on criminal convictions and offences is allowed only under official authority or when authorised by law with appropriate safeguards.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-10-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Data protection by design and by default
articles.summary: Controllers apply technical and organisational measures so that data protection principles are built in and only necessary data are processed by default.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-25-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Processor
articles.summary: Processing by a processor requires a binding contract with the required terms, and only processors that offer sufficient guarantees may be used.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-28-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Records of processing activities (controller)
articles.summary: The controller records purposes, data categories, recipients, transfers, retention limits and security measures; retention and security items apply where possible.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-30-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Exemption from the records duty
articles.summary: The records duty is waived for organisations under 250 employees, unless processing is not occasional, risks people's rights, or covers special categories or criminal data.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-30-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Security of processing
articles.summary: Controller and processor implement security measures appropriate to the risk, such as pseudonymisation, encryption, resilience and regular testing.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-32-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Breach notification to the authority
articles.summary: A personal data breach is notified to the supervisory authority within 72 hours, unless it is unlikely to result in a risk to people.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-33-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Data protection impact assessment
articles.summary: A DPIA is carried out before processing that is likely to result in a high risk to rights and freedoms, especially with new technologies.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-35-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Minimum content of a DPIA
articles.summary: A DPIA contains a description of the processing and its purposes, an assessment of necessity and proportionality, a risk assessment and the measures to address the risks.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-35-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: General principle for transfers
articles.summary: Transfers to third countries are allowed only if the conditions of the transfer chapter are met, so that the level of protection is not undermined.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-44-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Transfers on the basis of an adequacy decision
articles.summary: A transfer may take place to a country, territory or sector that the Commission has found to ensure an adequate level of protection.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-45-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards
articles.summary: Without an adequacy decision, transfers need appropriate safeguards, such as standard contractual clauses or binding corporate rules, with enforceable rights.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-46-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Binding corporate rules
articles.summary: Supervisory authorities approve binding corporate rules for transfers within a group of undertakings when the requirements are met.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-47-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Derogations for specific situations
articles.summary: Specific situations allow transfers without adequacy or safeguards, such as explicit consent after being informed of the risks.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-49-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Administrative fines, lower tier
articles.summary: Fines of up to EUR 10,000,000 or 2% of worldwide annual turnover for infringements of, among others, articles 8, 11, 25 to 39, 42 and 43.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-83-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Administrative fines, upper tier
articles.summary: Fines of up to EUR 20,000,000 or 4% of worldwide annual turnover for infringements of articles 5, 6, 7 and 9, data subject rights and transfers (44 to 49).
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/art-83-gdpr/ on 2026-10-08; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Specific protection of children
articles.summary: Children merit specific protection of their personal data, particularly for marketing, profiling and services offered directly to a child.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/recitals/no-38/ on 2026-10-14; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.

articles.title: Risks to the rights and freedoms of people
articles.summary: Describes risks of varying likelihood and severity, including processing the personal data of vulnerable natural persons, in particular children.
articles.verificationNote: Read on the unofficial mirror https://gdpr-info.eu/recitals/no-75/ on 2026-10-14; the official EUR-Lex text still needs the manual check described in docs/legal-sources.md.
